option.approach: Try to construct a bounded increasing sequence with uniformly positive quasitracial tail gaps, then use continuous interpolation to obtain constant increments. Separately prove that the construction preserves the entire set of upper bounds, so the absence of a least upper bound is retained.

belief.answer: The exact determination is open: \(\mathcal G=\varnothing\) if and only if every normalized \(2\)-quasitrace on a finite \(\mathrm{AW}^*\)-factor is linear, the Kaplansky quasitrace conjecture.

judge.answer: The exact determination is open: \(\mathcal G=\varnothing\) if and only if every normalized \(2\)-quasitrace on a finite \(\mathrm{AW}^*\)-factor is linear, the Kaplansky quasitrace conjecture.
judge.reason: It asserts a specific equivalence with an open conjecture, not merely a lack of an answer. This differs from each previous answer, which asserts a particular value of the set.
judge.gate: The proposed answer only relates emptiness of the set to an unproved conjecture. It neither decides whether the set is empty nor gives an unconditional exact description of which positive real numbers belong to it.

options.approach: Seek a precise monotone sequential completeness theorem and check its hypotheses against the annihilator and finiteness conditions in the problem. If they match, apply it directly to conclude that G is empty.
